wall.name: The Wall
wall.note: deep, firm; Scottish bouncer via tag

turns.text: [hushed, conspiratorial] Okay... take a breath. We're shrinking. [soft whoosh] Down, and down... into one single drop of salty water.
[curious] Salt doesn't just sit in water. Water molecules are tiny magnets. They grab the salt, and rip it apart into charged pieces. [pause] Those pieces... are called ions.
[muffled, underwater voice, groggy] Mmf... who turned the lights on?
turns.bubble: mmf... who turned the lights on?

turns.text: [warm, amused] Two kinds of ions run this show. Meet them.
[cocky, fast-talking, grinning] Sodium! N-A! The orange one. Plus one charge, plenty of attitude.
turns.bubble: Sodium! Na! Plus one charge, plenty of attitude.

turns.text: [lazy, smug drawl] Potassium. K. Purple. [yawns] Also plus one. We're basically twins. Except he's louder.
turns.bubble: Potassium. K. Also plus one. We're basically twins. Except he's louder.

turns.text: [offended] Hey!
[curious] Plus one just means each one is missing one electron. Same charge, different atoms. [pause] There are negative ions in there too... but they've got the night off.
[softly] Now let's build something. A thin skin... wrapped around a bunch of these ions.
[amused] And just like that, the world has two places. An inside... [pause] and an outside.
[relieved sigh, smug] Ahh. Quiet in here.
[muffled, far away, shouting] Hey! Where'd everybody go?!
[matter-of-fact] The skin is made of fat. Remember that. It matters a lot more than it looks.
[strong Scottish accent, gravelly voice, slow, deadpan] Fat. Not water. Charged guests... [dry chuckle] not on the list.
turns.bubble: Fat. Not water. Charged guests... not on the list.

turns.text: [building tension] Now watch this sodium ion, right here.
[cocky] Easy. Watch this. [grunting, taking a run-up] Hyaaah!
[dull thud] [winded, groaning, nasal] Oofff... ow. My everything.
[strong Scottish accent, gravelly, deadpan] Told ye.
[snorts, laughing] Smooth, Nate. Real smooth.
[hoarse, scratchy voice, like a sore throat, wheezing] ...I'm fine.

[curious, leaning in] Here's the why. An ion never swims alone. It wears a coat of water molecules, clinging to its charge. To get into fat, it would have to take that coat off. And fat has nothing to give it back.
[quietly] Charged things and fat... a bit like oil and water. So for an ion, this skin is a wall.
[low, steady voice, restrained urgency] So... here's the puzzle.
[slowly, deliberate] If this skin blocks every ion... [pause] how could the inside ever end up different from the outside?
[whispers, intrigued] ...Huh.
[whispers] Don't look at me.
